question: Using Figure 2A-1 and Section 2A.11, describe the requirements for a retroreflective strip used on a sign support to enhance conspicuity.
model_answer: Direct Answer: A retroreflective strip on a sign support is one of the permitted methods (based on engineering judgment) for enhancing sign conspicuity. When used, it is mandatory that the strip be at least 2 inches wide, run the full length of the support from the sign to within 2 feet above the near edge of the roadway, match the sign's background color (except red for YIELD and DO NOT ENTER signs), and carry no legend or other information. A related mandatory application exists for Crossbuck supports at passive grade crossings, where a white strip is required on the back of the support. Standards (mandatory): - "If a strip of retroreflective material is used on the sign support, it shall be at least 2 inches in width, it shall be placed for the full length of the support from the sign to within 2 feet above the near edge of the roadway, and its color shall match the background color of the sign, except that the color of the strip for the YIELD and DO NOT ENTER signs shall be red. The retroreflective strip shall not display any legend or other information." - For passive grade crossings: "A vertical strip of retroreflective white material, not less than 2 inches in width, shall be used on each Crossbuck support at passive grade crossings for the full length of the back of the support from the Crossbuck sign or Number of Tracks plaque to within 2 feet above the near edge of the roadway, except as provided in Paragraph 18 of this Section." Options (permitted): - Based upon engineering judgment, where improvement of the conspicuity of a standard regulatory, warning, or guide sign is desired, various methods may be used as appropriate (see Figure 2A-1), including a vertical retroreflective strip on the sign support. Visual evidence: - [Image 1] Figure 2A-1, panel E, illustrates a "Vertical retroreflective strip on sign support" beneath a fluorescent yellow-green pedestrian warning sign assembly, with the strip color matching the sign background and a "2 ft MAX." dimension shown from the bottom of the strip to the near edge of the roadway. - [Image 2] shows the same Figure 2A-1 page (p.48) with panel E depicting the strip running the full length of the support down to within 2 feet of the roadway edge. - [Image 3] shows Section 2A.21 (p.62), which notes that information regarding the use of retroreflective material on the sign support is contained in Section 2A.11. - [Image 4] shows the Section 2A.11 text (p.49), including method L (adding a strip of retroreflective material to the sign support) and the Standard in Paragraph 5. - [Image 5] shows Figure 8B-2 (Crossbuck Assembly), depicting a "2-inch white retroreflective strip on back of support" and an "Optional 2-inch red or white retroreflective strip on front of support," ending "2 ft MAX." above the edge of the roadway. Citations: - Section 2A.11 Standard §5 (p.49) - Section 2A.11 Option §1 (p.49) - Section 8B.04 Standard §17 (p.1000) - Section 2A.21 Support §8 (p.62) - Figure 2A-1 (p.48)
gold_answer: The strip must be at least 2 inches wide, extend from the sign down the full support to within 2 feet above the near edge of the roadway, match the sign background color except that YIELD and DO NOT ENTER strips are red, and contain no legend or other information.
